title: Isolation and separation of murine tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) subpopulations from orthotopic 4T1 breast tumors
protocol: Use healthy, 9–12-weeks-old female BALB/c mice for the experiment.
Remove the fur around and below the right nipple of the 4th mammary gland of each mouse by depilation or shaving, to expose the injection site.
Culture Mus musculus 4T1 mammary gland cancer cells in complete DMEM media in a humidified incubator in 5% CO2 at 37°C under sterile conditions.
Subculture the cells when they reach 80% confluence using a subcultivation ratio of 1:5.
Passage thawed cells at least twice before injecting them into mice.
Remove the medium from cell culture flasks, quickly rinse the cells with PBS and incubate them with 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA solution at 37°C until they detach.
Add fresh culture medium and collect the cells into 50 mL falcons.
Spin down for 5 min at 300 g and wash the cell pellets twice in PBS by means of centrifugation (5 min, 300 g) to completely wash away the cell culture medium.
Resuspend the pellets in PBS at a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells per 50 μL.
Keep the cellular suspensions on ice at all times.
Prepare an excess volume of cell suspension (10%–20%) for injections.
Inject 1 × 10^6 cells into the right nipple of the 4th mammary gland.
Hold the syringe with the needle tip turned upwards to enter the skin subcutaneously at 10 mm from the inoculation nipple, between the 4th and 5th mammary glands.
Move the needle along the skin towards the inoculation nipple until the tip is right under that nipple.
Move the needle slightly in all directions around the nipple (within a 3 mm radius) while holding it parallel to the skin.
Carefully move the needle tip up into the mammary fat pad till the needle eye comes under the nipple tip.
Inject cells at once, but slowly, so that a visible flat thickening forms around the nipple.
Turn the needle 45 degrees to the right and slowly pull it out while still pressing on the plunger.
Measure tumor growth with a caliper, 3 times per week for up to 24 days.
Proceed when tumors reach the growth endpoint or a desired size.
Sacrifice tumor-bearing mice using an approved method by an ethical committee of your institution.
Collect tumors immediately in cold PBS.
Separate the draining lymph node from the tumor.
Chop each tumor into 2–4 mm pieces with a scalpel.
Transfer chopped tissue into a gentleMACS C Tube containing 5 mL of sterile digestion buffer.
Dissolve powders for collagenase type I, dispase type I, and DNAse I stock in advance.
Pass the dissolved powders and DNase I through a 0.22 μm filter immediately before use.
Add the filtered mixture to the digestion buffer.
Tightly close the C Tube and attach it upside down onto the sleeve of the gentleMACS Octo Dissociator.
Ensure that the sample is located in the area of the rotor/stator, covered with digestion buffer, and free from tumor pieces on the tube walls.
Run the gentleMACS program suitable for hard tumors (e.g., ‘37C_m_TDK_2’).
For softer tumors (e.g., E0771 mammary tumors), run the ‘37C_m_TDK_1’ program.
Mince tumors in 5 mL RPMI medium containing 0.1% collagenase type I and 0.2% dispase type I using a scalpel.
Maintain tumor pieces in the same digestion solution for 30 min at 37°C, vortexing every 5 min.
Transfer each sample to ice exactly after 30 min of digestion.
Add 10 mL of FACS buffer into the gentleMACS C Tube containing the digested tissue.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer placed on a 50 mL tube.
Wash the strainer with FACS buffer to achieve a uniform final volume of 30–40 mL in each tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 350 g.
Discard the supernatant carefully to avoid disrupting the pellets.
Incubate the resulting pellets in 1 mL red blood cell lysis buffer for 3 min at 37°C.
Immediately place the samples on ice and resuspend them in 10 mL FACS buffer.
Pipette up and down and pass through a 40 μm cell strainer placed on a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 350 g.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL FACS buffer.
Calculate the number of viable cells in each sample using a counting chamber and a light microscope.

Resuspend each sample in the blocking solution (dilute the Fc block CD16/CD32 antibody in the FACS buffer at a ratio of 1:25, i.e., 4 μL of antibody in 96 μL of FACS buffer) in the following ratio: 1 × 10^6 cells per 10 μL of blocking solution.
Transfer the samples to FACS tubes.
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Collect a small equal volume (e.g., 10 μL) from each sample.
Pool the collected volumes in FACS tubes for controls.
Note down the final volumes of Unstained Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls.
Prepare a 2× concentrated master mix of appropriate antibodies/dyes in an Eppendorf tube.
To each sample (cells in blocking solution), add the same volume of the 2× concentrated master mix to achieve a final concentration of 1×.
Vortex briefly and incubate for 20 min at 4°C, protected from light.
Centrifuge (5 min, 350 g) after incubation.
Resuspend pellets in 3 mL PBS.
Centrifuge again (5 min, 350 g) to wash the samples.
Resuspend pellets in FACS buffer at a concentration of 20 million cells per 1000 μL.
Keep samples at 4°C and protected from light until detection and sorting.
Add the volume of FACS buffer equal to the sample volume for unstained controls.
Vortex briefly and incubate for 20 min at 4°C (protected from light).
Keep at 4°C protected from light until detection.
Prepare a 2× concentrated staining mix for each FMO control, excluding one antibody.
Add the volume of 2× mix to each FMO control equal to its sample volume.
Vortex briefly and incubate for 20 min at 4°C (protected from light).
Centrifuge for 5 min at g speed.
Resuspend pellets in 3 ml PBS.
Centrifuge again for 5 min at 350 g to wash the samples.
Resuspend pellets in 100-200 μL of FACS buffer.
Keep at 4°C protected from light until detection.
Use UltraComp beads or equivalent beads following manufacturer’s instructions for fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies.
For viability dye, take an aliquot and incubate at 65°C for 1 min to kill cells.
Place cells on ice immediately afterward.
Mix equal volumes of viable and heat-killed cells.
Spin down and wash once with FACS buffer.
Incubate the cell mixture with a viability dye diluted in FACS buffer for 20 min on ice protected from light.
Wash the cells twice with FACS buffer to remove excessive viability dye.
Prepare cell collection tubes containing 4 mL of sterile complete RPMI medium and store them on ice.
Collect cells using the BD FACSAria™ III Cell Sorter with BD FACSDivaTM software.
Select parameters including FSC-A, FSC-W, FSC-H, SSC-A, SSC-W, SSC-H, eFluor-506 (viability), eFluor-450 (CD11b), AlexaFluor488 (F4/80), PE (PDPN).
Set appropriate photomultiplier tubes voltages for FSC-A and SSC-A parameters using the unstained control.
Calculate the compensation matrix with single stained compensation controls.
Use the unstained or appropriate FMO control to create gates for various populations of interest.
Gate total TAMs as single, viable, CD11b+, and F4/80+ cells.
Gate PoEMs as single, viable, CD11b+, F4/80+, and PDPN+ cells.
Gate non-PoEMs as single, viable, CD11b+, F4/80+, and PDPN- cells.
Sort different TAM populations into corresponding collection tubes containing 4 mL of sterile complete RPMI medium.
Store isolated cells on ice for up to 2 hours.
Keep sorting and collection tubes at 4°C during the sorting process.
Use a 100 μm nozzle and sort at a flow rate of 1-3.
Process sorted cells within a 2-hour timeframe, in parallel with ongoing sorting.
Wash the collected cells with PBS.
Culture the cells in DMEM complete medium in Sterilin 30 mm Petri Dishes at a density of 0.5 million cells per dish or in 96-well cell culture plates at up to 3 × 10^4 cells per well.
Alternatively, spin down the cells for 5 minutes at 300 g.
Wash the spun-down cells with PBS for 5 minutes at 300 g.
Aspirate and remove the supernatant.
Collect the cells in RLT lysis buffer according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Store the collected sample immediately at -80°C until RNA isolation.
